# sentry_project_inbound_filter (Resource)

One of a project's built-in inbound data filters, which drop events before they count against the quota. Every project has all of them, so creating this resource takes the filter over and destroying it turns the filter off.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "sentry_project_inbound_filter" "crawlers" {
  project_id = sentry_project.api.id
  filter_id  = "web-crawlers"
  active     = true
}

# The legacy browsers filter takes the browsers to filter instead of a switch.
resource "sentry_project_inbound_filter" "legacy_browsers" {
  project_id = sentry_project.api.id
  filter_id  = "legacy-browsers"
  subfilters = ["ie", "opera_mini"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `filter_id` (String) The filter: `browser-extensions`, `localhost`, `web-crawlers`, `filtered-transaction` (health check transactions) or `legacy-browsers`.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project, e.g. `sentry_project.example.id`.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the filter is on. Required for every filter except `legacy-browsers`, which takes `subfilters` instead.
- `subfilters` (Set of String) Only for `legacy-browsers`, and required there: the browsers whose old versions are filtered, e.g. `ie`, `edge`, `safari`, `firefox`, `chrome`, `opera`, `android`, `opera_mini`. An empty set turns the filter off.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<project_id>/<filter_id>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by <project slug or ID>/<filter ID>.
terraform import sentry_project_inbound_filter.crawlers api/web-crawlers
```
